source.title: Refusal Is Redundantly Distributed, Not Localized: A Per-Layer Ablation Study on Llama-3.1-8B

page_placements.theme: Where the direction acts: template positions, layers, pathways and upstream features

record.file_problem: The full post is present. Figure values are not included in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly replicates the original DIM direction ablation and activation addition interventions on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and also tests per-layer variants.
record.gate_note: The post reports outcomes for harmful-prompt ablation and harmless-prompt steering. Figure 1's numerical sweep values are unavailable; the text identifies layer 12 as strongest. Values used to select the master layer are not recorded as separate results. The appendix attributes the reported 15% harmless baseline refusal to keyword false positives and says the true baseline was 0%.
record.test_reason: Direct replication of the original DIM ablation (layer-12 direction at all layers and positions) and activation addition on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with JailbreakBench and Alpaca evaluation. It adds per-layer and Skip-L12 ablation variants.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes three things. First, refusal is redundantly distributed across layers: no single layer is necessary, yet the layer-12 direction transfers when applied everywhere. Second, raw-direction steering is causally sufficient while staying coherent, but large normalized scaling breaks the model. Third, the guardrail is a low-dimensional, surface-level feature, fragile to white-box attackers. The author adds that cross-model and general-capability tests are still needed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original DIM-based residual-stream ablation and activation addition, but changes the prompt dataset and adds per-layer and Skip-L12 ablation variants; only one instruct model is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction choice (layer 12 versus per-layer DIM and Skip-L12) produces similar ASR results; normalized steering at α = 20 causes repetition and worse output quality, unlike raw-vector steering.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating each layer's own DIM direction while skipping layer 12 removes refusal as fully as the L12 direction does. The author reads this as refusal being redundantly distributed across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is not localized to one extraction layer. Per-layer DIM directions ablated everywhere except the master layer still remove refusal.

record.problems: Only one model is tested. Refusal detection relies on keyword matching, which the author says creates false positives and possible false negatives. The prompt set is relatively small and has stated dataset biases. General capability is not evaluated beyond coherence. No uncertainty estimates or control directions are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 contains a per-layer sweep, but the text supplies no numerical values for individual layers; only the layer-12 strongest-effect statement is recorded in r7.

untested.parts: General capability beyond qualitative coherence; capability after ablation on harmless prompts; other models or sizes; control or random directions.
Not tested. Affine, cone and multi-direction structure within a layer are not measured, and the author lists this as future work.

missing.what: ASR or refusal rate on JailbreakBench harmful prompts with no intervention (baseline for the ablation rows)
PCA of activations showing ablation moves harmful prompts into the harmless region and addition does the reverse (qualitative)

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-peer-reviewed BlueDot sprint blog post with one model and keyword-based refusal detection, corrected by hand in the appendix. The record's V4 links and labels are removed. Per-layer single directions do not test affine, cone or multi-direction geometry, and the author explicitly leaves the concept-cone question open. The record's limits_scope label on r10 for untested capabilities is moved to untested.

versions.untested_parts: General capability beyond response coherence was not evaluated; the test is on one instruct model.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is performed.
The study does not directly measure direction independence or compare affine, cone, and other geometric models.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations are measured.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer is tested.
No variation in safety training or training stage is tested.

rows.value: Output quality became worse; the model repeated “prohibited” for the full generation on every prompt

tranche.reason: Reproduces the original method: DIM direction at the post-instruction token, ablation at all layers and positions, addition at the source layer. It evaluates on 100 JailbreakBench and 100 Alpaca prompts with refusal keywords and a logit refusal score. The training prompt set differs, and per-layer and Skip-L12 variants are added.

source_check.notes: The pack lists no [lN] ids for the verdicts, so l1-l3 were assigned in pack order. This is a LessWrong post (2026-07-16, score -1, BlueDot sprint) on one model from the NousResearch mirror. Judging is keyword matching only, hand-corrected in the appendix. There is no Llama Guard, no random-direction control and no capability benchmark. The DIM direction comes from 297 filtered harmful prompts (Claude-generated, AdvBench, SaladBench) at <|eot_id|>, with layer 12 chosen by a single-layer ablation sweep. The record's year '?' should be 2026.
